hints: Look carefully at where D sits in the Venn diagram. It is right in the centre, so ask yourself what it means for a property to be there.
Do not count only C=C bonds. Remember to also count the C=O double bond in a carboxyl group (-COOH) and the many C=O groups in peptide bonds.
walkthrough:
**Understand what D means**

Great start. The three circles are unsaturated fatty acid, collagen and haemoglobin.

Region D is the overlap of all three circles, so it means a feature shared by all three types of molecule.

**Count double bonds in an unsaturated fatty acid**

An unsaturated fatty acid has at least one C=C between carbons in its hydrocarbon chain.

It also has a carboxyl group with one C=O, so total is at least two:
$$1 \times (C=C) + 1 \times (C=O) = at least \ 2 \ double \ bonds$$

**Count double bonds in collagen and haemoglobin**

Both collagen and haemoglobin are proteins made of many amino acids joined by peptide bonds.

Each amino acid residue contributes a C=O from the backbone, so a whole protein chain has hundreds of double bonds, well over two.

**Put it together**

Since all three molecule types have at least two double bonds, the property belongs in the centre where all three overlap.

That is region D, so D is the answer.

options.A: Region A is shared only by unsaturated fatty acid and haemoglobin, not collagen. Having at least two double bonds is true for collagen too, so it cannot be A.
options.B: Region B is shared only by collagen and haemoglobin, not unsaturated fatty acid. An unsaturated fatty acid also has at least two double bonds, so it cannot be B.
options.C: Region C is shared only by unsaturated fatty acid and collagen, not haemoglobin. Haemoglobin also has many double bonds in its peptide bonds, so it cannot be C.
options.D: Region D is shared by all three. Unsaturated fatty acids have C=C plus C=O, and both proteins have many C=O in peptide bonds, so all contain at least two double bonds.
